hook_text: One flat sheet of paper cannot hold a single coin. Fold it the right way and it holds a whole pile.
clip_script: One sheet of paper. One gap. How many coins? Flat sheet: it sags before the first coin even lands! Now fold it into a zigzag. Coin, coin, coin, more than twenty! Roll it into tubes. Strong! Glue layers together. Stiff! Copy the wavy layer inside a cardboard box. Light and tough! Same paper every time. Only the shape changed. Strong shapes make strong structures.
visual_style: Whiteboard sheet of paper sagging between two books, then the same sheet folded into a zigzag holding a stack of coins, then rolled, layered and corrugated versions.
mood: Like a classroom challenge with a big reveal.
pacing: The floppy sheet first, then four ways to make it strong, each tested with coins.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a paper bridge that holds ten coins.
